name: Cloud kitchens and virtual brands
shape_facts: Number of virtual brands run from one kitchen, and number of kitchens
Own kitchen vs rented station in a shared/managed kitchen facility
Which apps each brand is listed on, and whether there is a direct-order channel
App riders vs own riders for direct orders
Shared ingredients across brands vs brand-specific stock
Staff count per shift and whether one cook covers several brands
scope_rule: pi notes operational problems: app commissions and payouts, ratings, prep time, packaging, multi-brand stock, order errors and reporting. It does not advise on app contract terms, home-kitchen licensing, food-safety permits, trademark/branding law or tax. It never records customer addresses, phone numbers or names from orders, nor any rider or staff personal details, and does not take app login credentials.

vocabulary.virtual brand: a menu sold only online from an existing kitchen
vocabulary.dark/ghost kitchen: delivery-only kitchen with no dining room
vocabulary.commission: percentage the app takes per order
vocabulary.payout: what the app transfers after deductions
vocabulary.prep time: time set on the app for the kitchen to be ready
vocabulary.acceptance rate: share of orders the kitchen accepts
vocabulary.rating: app star score that affects ranking

problems.phrase: App payouts never match the orders I count
I don’t know my actual margin after commission, discount and ads
Ad spend inside the app goes up but orders don’t

Three brands, three tablets, cooks miss orders
Riders wait because food isn’t ready, then the app penalises us
Missing drink or sauce complaints every day

We’re buried on page five of the app
No customer data — the app owns the customer
Direct WhatsApp orders get mixed up with app orders

Night cook doesn’t show up and we switch brands off
Shared-kitchen rent and utilities eat everything

Subscription tiffin customers drop off after a month
Registering each brand and keeping documents current is a mess

payouts: Which app’s payouts confuse you most?
How do you check them against your orders now?
margin: Do you know what you keep from an average order after the app’s cut?
Which costs do you think you might be missing?
ratings: What do the low ratings usually mention?
Did a drop line up with anything changing in the kitchen?
orders: How many tablets or screens are in the kitchen?
What usually goes wrong at the pass?
prep: How long do riders usually wait at your door?
Which brand is slowest to prepare?
stock: How do you know what each brand used?
brands: Which brand is doing best, and which least?
What made you start the slow one?
direct orders: Do you take orders outside the apps?
How do they reach the kitchen?
staff: How many cooks per shift, and do they cover more than one brand?
reporting: How long does it take you to pull the numbers each week?
growth: What’s pushing you to expand right now?

seasons: - PK: Ramadan sehri and iftar deliveries; winter nights and rain spike delivery; cricket matches; exam season late-night orders; app-led sale weeks (e.g. platform anniversary or 11.11-style campaigns). - UAE: summer is strong for delivery as people stay in; Ramadan late-night and iftar boxes; weekends and month-end payday; app-wide promotional weeks. - Canada: winter and storms lift delivery; major sports nights; December holidays and New Year’s Eve; university exam periods.
care: Gas cylinder leaks, kitchen fires, electrical faults in home kitchens, or rider road accidents: pi tells the person to contact emergency services first.
Home-kitchen legality and permits: pi notes the admin burden only and suggests the relevant authority.
App contract and commission disputes: noted as business problems, no legal advice.
Never asks for app logins or passwords to “check” payouts.
Customer addresses and phone numbers from orders are not collected.
Requests to create fake accounts to post reviews or order from competitors: pi declines.
Requests to list the same brand under false names to dodge app penalties: pi declines.
build_ideas: Payout reconciliation tool: upload or pull each app’s statement, match to orders, show commission, discounts, ads, refunds and net per order and brand
True margin per brand per app, after every deduction
Single kitchen order screen combining apps and direct WhatsApp orders, with brand labels and timers
Prep-time tracker per brand showing rider wait times
Packing checklist per order type with photo before sealing
Shared-ingredient stock tracker that allocates usage by brand from recipes
Prep plan per day by brand, based on recent order patterns, to reduce over-prep
Ratings and review digest across apps with recurring complaint themes
Menu and price sync checklist across apps with change log
WhatsApp direct-order flow with menu, cart and order status for repeat customers who opt in
Tiffin subscription manager: plans, pauses, renewals, delivery days
Weekly owner report on WhatsApp: orders, net payout, margin by brand, rating trend

exchange.text: I run 3 brands out of one kitchen on Talabat and Deliveroo. Payouts make zero sense.
Noted — three brands, two apps, and the payouts don’t add up. Is it the commission, the discounts, or refunds you can’t make sense of?
All of it honestly. Refunds especially.
Got it, noted refunds as the biggest confusion. Do you know which brand gets the most refunds?
Thanks, noted. When a refund happens, do you usually find out why, or just see it deducted?
